title: Track Composition (ordered, low-collision issue lanes)
description: Track composition for the orchestrate setup flow, written to .worktrees/.status/tracks.json. A track is an ORDERED sequence of low-collision issues run serially in one lane; the setup flow proposes 2-4 tracks (composed by orchestrate/workflow.js `mode: "tracks"`, pure computation) and the operator approves them and picks the run's autonomy level (L1-L4). AUTHORITATIVE for track membership + within-track ordering + the chosen per-track autonomy_level. PR/MR state and issue status labels remain authoritative for golem liveness. Sibling to pool-status.schema.json, golem-status.schema.json, and agent-status.schema.json.

tracks.description: The composed tracks, in lane order. Each track's issues run serially (issue k+1 dispatches after issue k's PR merges), so within-track collisions are moot and cross-track overlap was minimized at composition.

lane.description: 0-based lane index. One golem runs per track head; the rest of the track queues behind it.

autonomy_level.description: The rules-of-engagement level (L1-L4) chosen at setup for this track, per orchestrate/autonomy-levels.md. A track containing a severity/critical issue is capped at L3. Set by the setup flow (issue #178 Part B); the pure `tracks` composition step does not populate it.

issues.description: Issue numbers in serial execution order (the head is issues[0]). Composition preserves next-issue priority order within the lane.

head.description: DISPLAY CACHE: the issue currently dispatched (or last dispatched) for this lane. The live golem set is authoritative via PR/label state; lane-aware refill advances this as each issue's PR merges.

dispatched.description: Whether this lane's head has been dispatched. Written by the `--runbook` setup-flow variant (issue #673), which composes and banks a plan WITHOUT dispatching: every lane starts `false` and flips to `true` as the operator hand-launches that lane's head from the runbook. Absent means dispatched (back-compat: every tracks.json written before #673 came from a dispatching setup flow). What makes a partially-executed plan render correctly — an in-flight lane shows as such instead of re-offering its launch command.

deps_honored.description: DISPLAY ONLY: build-order dependency edges (issue #462) co-located and ordered within this lane, e.g. ["#19->#22", "#20->#22"] meaning #19/#20 were placed ahead of #22 because #22 depends on them. Emitted by orchestrate/workflow.js `mode: "tracks"` (composeTracks), derived purely from each backlog item's `deps` array — the edges whose BOTH endpoints landed in this lane. (The setup flow resolves `deps` from `Depends on #N` / `Blocked by #N` / native blockedBy before calling the composer; composeTracks itself stays pure and only reads the resolved `deps`.) Shown so the operator sees why a lane is ordered as it is. Optional — a lane with no in-lane dependency edge omits it.

deferred.description: Backlog issues that did not fit any track this composition (all lanes full or capped), in priority order. A later composition sweep can pick them up.

dispatched.description: Whether this composition has been dispatched at all. `false` marks a PLANNED-NOT-DISPATCHED plan banked by the `--runbook` setup-flow variant (issue #673) for the operator to hand-launch one lane at a time. Absent means dispatched (back-compat). Re-running `/workflow:orchestrate tracks --runbook` against a `false` plan RE-RENDERS the banked runbook rather than recomposing — the backlog may have moved, and a plan the operator is halfway through executing must not be reshuffled underneath them; recomposition is available but explicit.

rationale.description: DISPLAY ONLY: short, deterministic, data-derived notes explaining the composition (lane count / sizes / co-located dependency clusters / any cycle or oversized-cluster split / out-of-backlog dep refs / deferred count / overlap). Emitted by orchestrate/workflow.js `mode: "tracks"` (composeTracks) and shown in the proposal the operator approves. Persisted so a banked `--runbook` plan can render it days later without recomposing — the operator decides WHICH lane is worth spending on, which needs the reasoning, not just the lane contents.

cross_track_overlap.description: Count of unordered lane pairs that share >= 1 predicted file. Lower is better — the composition minimizes this so serial tracks stay merge-independent.

updated.description: ISO datetime of the last tracks.json write.
